Mira_CS: Hey team - onboarding note from Lina: embedded client spiking 429s when we ramp their background workers. Happened right after they enabled parallel prefetch. Any quick wins?

Jon_Integration: Do we have the rate-limit headers from the gateway or client logs? rough RPS pattern?

Mira_CS: Pasted logs from Lina below (sanitized):
Lina: 2026-03-21T10:12:02Z GET /v1/generate 200 x-token-ms=15 x-rate-limit-limit=100 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=13
Lina: 2026-03-21T10:12:03Z POST /v1/generate 429 x-rate-limit-limit=100 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=12

Sam_SRE: Looks like they hit the per-minute window. Remaining = 0 in header, reset in ~12s. Are they using ephemeral tokens that preflight multiple times? Might be preflight concurrency fanout.

Jon_Integration: If they're using the embedded SDK default, preflight happens per worker process. We should recommend connection pooling + shared ephemeral token refresh. Also enable client-side leaky-bucket smoothing. Example config we can ask them to try:

```js
// client-side smoothing example
const client = new RedwoodEmbed({
  maxConcurrency: 8,        // cap concurrent requests
  tokenRefreshWorkers: 1,   // single token refresher shared across workers
  requestBurstTolerance: 20 // queue bursts locally
});
```

Mira_CS: Sent that snippet to Lina. She said they spawn 16 workers and each does a preflight check -> 16x preflight at startup.

Sam_SRE: We can also add a soft-cap in the gateway: detect many preflight checks from same API key/conn and serialise for 15s. But that's an infra change. Short term: ask them to stagger starts and reuse connection.

Jon_Integration: Another quick mitigation: switch to async token refresh with jittered backoff and memoize the token per process for 30s. Also suggest exponential backoff on 429 with Retry-After respect.

Mira_CS: Lina tried setting maxConcurrency to 6 and enabling tokenRefreshWorkers:1. After that the 429s dropped to 1/min for a few minutes while their backlog drained.

Lina (via Mira_CS): "the fix worked, thanks! can you suggest a recommended startup pattern so we don't hit this on future deploys?"

Jon_Integration: Recommend: start workers in waves of N (e.g., 4), warm a shared connection, then gradually ramp. Also include this snippet for staggered startups:

```bash
# staggered startup in bash
for i in $(seq 1 16); do
  sleep $((i % 4)) && spawn-worker &
done
```

Sam_SRE: I'll file a small infra task to consider client-side preflight coalescing at the edge and an opt-in soft-throttle for new API keys. For now: CS to document the onboarding checklist (maxConcurrency, shared token refresher, staggered start) and add it to the onboarding playbook.

Mira_CS: Filing checklist doc link: https://docs.redwood.ai/onboard/embedded-sdk-concurrency (placeholder). Closing loop with Lina and scheduling a follow-up in 48h. :white_check_mark:
